newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO VIEW - Fewer China plays to boost local firms.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW - Fewer China plays to boost local firms.

text.p: Fewer initial public offerings (IPO) of hot China plays this month should boost the trading debuts of local firms, analysts said.
Only three local companies are expected to launch IPOs in April, followed by seven to eight China plays from May onward.
"The absence of big fund-raising exercises by red chips and H-shares can aid the subscription response (for local companies)," said Michael Ng, an analyst at ASG Investment.
Red chips are Hong Kong companies with strong China ties, while H-shares are Hong Kong-listed shares in China-incorporated enterprises.
With some confusion in the Hong Kong market about whether red chip companies need approval from China to list here, analysts said some China plays had delayed their IPO plans.
Rumours spread around the market in late March that GITIC Enterprises Ltd's IPO was almost scuttled because it had not obtained necessary approvals from Chinese authorities.
The listing went through successfully but the rumours were never clarified, and the subsequent pause in new China-play listings has allowed local companies to grab the limelight.
Despite the generally weak tone in the Hong Kong stock market recently, analysts also said they were encouraged by the continued strong performances of new listings.
"Local sentiment towards IPOs is still very strong," said Tony Yung, head of research of Tai Fook Securities.
"Very few people have burnt their fingers in the IPO market so far and that is likely to build up confidence," he said, adding investors would continue to seek quick, hefty profits.
Shares of electronic component maker Wing Lee Holdings Ltd ended their debut at HK$1.53 (US$0.20) last Thursday, up 53 percent from an issue price of HK$1.00.
Shares of KEL Holdings Ltd, an electrical and mechnical engineering concern, are due to begin trading on April 24.
The company, a spinoff of UDL Holdings Ltd, is issuing 100 million new shares at HK$1 each. Its IPO will close on April 15.
Market sources said Pacific Ports Co, a port projects operator and spinoff of Fairyoung Holdings Ltd, is expected to issue 200 million shares at HK$2.60 to HK$3.24 each.
Toy cars and electrical appliances manufacturer Kin Yat Holdings Ltd is expected to issue 85 million new shares at HK$1.28, market sources said.
